title: Learn2Synth: Learning Optimal Data Synthesis Using Hypergradients for Brain Image Segmentation
mechanism: Learn the parameters of a synthesis or augmentation engine by hypergradients, so a segmenter trained on synthetic or augmented data is optimal on a small real labelled set that is never trained on directly.
adaptation: Engine = about 10 parametric EL augmentations (crack-region contrast, blur matching the 4 px FWHM, scuff-streak overlay, half-cut masking, per-source gamma). Outer objective = soft crack IoU on val 54 + F51 (+ H36 for half-cut). After the search, fix the parameters and run a full house training.
min_experiment: Arm: house net trained with the learned augmentation parameters, 5 seeds. Baseline: house with label-safe augmentation. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 (primary), test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 below house + 0.02, or test crack IoU down by more than 0.012.
evidence: R: brain MRI synthetic-to-real; learned parametric and nonparametric synthesis beat hand-tuned domain randomization on synthetic and real scans (numbers not read; abstract only).
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF lists physics-based and generative synthesis as untried. Synthetic half-cut views were tried with hand-set parameters (n.d.); learned parameters are open.
